# Shared OAuth authorization server core

`github.com/Usefused/fused-open-core/oauthserver` is a separate Go module. It owns client registration, authorization-code and PKCE validation, consent, token issuance, refresh rotation, revocation, and cleanup. Fused and Threadify can use the same implementation while supplying different identities and scopes.

## Host contract

Construct `Service[ID]` with four dependencies:

- `Store[ID]` persists clients, consents, codes, and token families. Its methods must preserve the atomicity documented in `types.go`: consent and code issuance commit together; code exchange is single use; refresh rotation detects replay and revokes the token family. Store only hashes, never raw secrets.
- `RevisionSink` notifies the host when grants or clients change so cached authorization can be invalidated.
- `ScopeCatalog` validates product scope names. For every browser request, `Actor[ID].CanGrant` checks that the signed-in user currently holds each requested scope. A missing or failing callback denies the grant.
- `Prefixes` distinguishes credentials issued by each product. Fused retains its existing `foc_`, `fos_`, `foat_`, and `fort_` prefixes for compatibility. A Threadify adapter can choose its own prefixes.

`ID` is the host's comparable subject/credential identifier type. Fused uses `uuid.UUID`; Threadify can use its string IDs. Client IDs and grant row IDs remain UUIDs generated by the library.

The host mounts HTTP routes, authenticates browser sessions, enforces CSRF on consent, and renders consent and connected-app pages. When an OAuth access token reaches a product API, the host must verify the grant is active and enforce **granted token scope ∩ the user's current permissions ∩ resource access**. A token must never gain a permission merely because a role was added after consent. Fused's adapter lives in `internal/engine/oauthprovider`; its existing PostgreSQL tables and token prefixes remain compatible.

For local development, use a Go workspace containing this repository and the Engine checkout. Publish and tag this module only after both Engines use it.

## Tests

```sh
cd oauthserver && go test ./...
cd .. && go test ./internal/engine/oauthprovider ./internal/engine/store ./internal/engine/api -run OAuth
```
